title: Investigate kernel-route entropy causing intermittent throughput collapse and action plan
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: During a mid-February capacity upgrade and scheduler heuristic tweak we observed repeated, intermittent throughput collapses and p95+ tail latency spikes on several hosted clusters. The degradation manifested as ~40-70% drop in sustained tokens/s for short bursts and increased error budgets for some customers. This ticket documents the investigation, root cause hypothesis, and concrete action items to harden kernel selection and scheduler routing to avoid 'route entropy' when heuristics interact with quantized kernels.

Timeline and observed signals: 2025-02-10 02:14 UTC - first alert: sustained token throughput drop on cluster eu-west-1-prod; 02:18 - spike in scheduler route changes per minute; 02:25 - increase in RPC retries and dropped requests; 02:34 - partial rollback of scheduler heuristic reduced oscillation; 02:50 - metrics returned to baseline but residual tail latency observed.

Root cause (summary): A combination of a scheduler heuristic change that increased routing sensitivity to micro-latency variance and a newly-introduced quantized kernel with close performance characteristics produced non-deterministic kernel assignment across similar requests. Small perturbations caused the scheduler to frequently switch affinity, invalidating KV cache locality and causing batch fragmentation. The net effect was increased per-request overhead, reduced batching efficiency, and cache miss amplification (we call this kernel-route entropy).

Evidence and artifacts: - Heap of traces and flamegraphs: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/eval/kernel-entropy-2025-02 - Incident timeline and alerts: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-2025-0210 - PRs: GH-Redwood/runtime#8745 (scheduler sensitivity rollback), GH-Redwood/runtime#8761 (kernel telemetry patch) - Perf benchmark snapshots before/after: gs://redwood-perf/2025/02/cluster-eu-west-1/benchmarks.csv

Impact: Affected hosted clusters and some Dedicated customers with mixed model variants. Estimated customer-facing latency/throughput regressions impacted beta and production customers during the window. No data loss or model correctness regressions were detected.

Decision log and trade-offs: We considered three remediation approaches: 1) always pin kernel per model-variant (strict affinity) - lowest oscillation but reduces ability to route to faster kernels under load; 2) introduce hysteresis and stability scoring in the scheduler - moderate complexity, preserves flexibility; 3) revert all recent scheduler heuristics (stopgap) - simplest short-term fix. We performed a rollback of the most aggressive heuristic as an emergency measure (see GH-Redwood/runtime#8745) and are pursuing option 2 as the long-term solution.

Proposed long-term mitigations (high level): - Deterministic kernel scoring: implement stable score composed of latency mean, variance, and observed batch amplification penalty. - Hysteresis and cooldown: require a minimum stable window and score delta before switching kernel affinity. - Batch/kv-aware routing: scheduler should factor KV cache locality and batch occupancy into routing score. - Canary and progressive rollout: add micro-canary to monitor entropy metrics (route-change-rate, cache-miss-rate) prior to global rollout. - Improved telemetry: new metrics and dashboard for kernel-route entropy, including per-model variant route-change-rate and kv-hit-cohort graphs. - Automated rollback rule: trigger revert when route-change-rate crosses threshold and p95 increases for 5m.

Acceptance criteria: 1) Route-change-rate reduced by >= 90% under synthetic jitter workload compared to pre-fix; 2) No regression in median throughput; 3) New telemetry shows stable KV hit rate during bursts; 4) Unit and integration tests for scheduler scoring landed; 5) Canary rollout plan documented in runbook and exercised.

References: Confluence incident writeup: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/RT/Kernel+Route+Entropy+Feb+2025
comments: 2025-02-12 - Maya Patel: Initial triage complete. Root cause points to scheduler sensitivity interacting with a quantized kernel. Assigned to Linh for investigation and proposed remediation. Links to traces and dashboards included.

2025-02-14 - Linh Tran: Reproduced noisy routing locally with a stress harness that adds micro-latency jitter. Confirmed KV cache locality drops when router oscillates between kernel variants. Experimented with simple 500ms cooldown and observed 62% reduction in route churn in test harness.

2025-02-18 - Rahul Banerjee (serving): Reviewed test harness results. Concern: cooldown may harm responsiveness during legitimate load shifts. Proposal: scoring + hysteresis with config knobs exposed per-deployment.
2025-02-20 - Design review (Ava Martinez): Dashboard mockups for entropy metrics approved. UX will surface route-change-rate and per-model route timelines.
2025-02-25 - PR GH-Redwood/runtime#8761 opened: kernel telemetry (per-request kernel-id tags) and a prototype scoring function. Requesting review from infra and runtime owners.
2025-03-01 - Security (Noah Kim): Reviewed proposed telemetry. No PII or customer data leaking; KMS integrations unaffected. Security review not required for these changes.

2025-03-03 - Linh Tran: Implemented scheduler hysteresis + KV-aware penalty in branch feature/entropy-mitigation. Benchmarks show route-change-rate down 92% under synthetic jitter and throughput within 2% of baseline.
2025-03-04 - Maya Patel: Marking this ticket in progress; follow-up tickets created for rollout (ENG-35402), long-term perf tests (ENG-35403), and runbook updates (ENG-35404).
